title: Timestral (arXiv abstract page)
note: Fetched. Report submitted 27 Oct 2026: four probabilistic forecasting models (5M, 28M, 123M, 209M parameters). States that the 209M and 123M models take the top two places on every metric of GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench. Weights on Hugging Face, inference code on GitHub.

title: Timestral (arXiv abstract page)
note: Fetched. Design as the abstract gives it: forecast tokens kept apart from a causally encoded context, known-future covariates supported natively, pretraining on synthetic data only, then post-training on a mix of real and synthetic data with longer context. No scores, datasets or dates of the real data on this page.

title: mistralai/Timestral-209M model card
note: Fetched (also a research source). 209M-parameter checkpoint: patch transformer, 24 layers, 32-step patches, context to 32,768 steps, 1,024 steps per forward pass with longer horizons rolled block by block on the median, 21 quantiles, past-only and known-future covariates (numeric or categorical), runs on CPU. Weights under a Modified MIT licence. Tech report listed as coming soon.

title: mistralai/Timestral-209M model card
note: Fetched. Card table for the 209M model: GIFT-Eval MASE 0.658, CRPS 0.446; TIME MASE 0.626, CRPS 0.522; fev-bench SQL skill 50.39, MASE skill 39.49. Each is ahead of t0-gamma (0.661, 0.452, 0.637, 0.534, 49.42, 37.99), TimesFM-3, Toto-2.0-2.5B and Chronos-2. A family table gives the 5M, 28M and 123M scores. No load task, no intervals, no test windows.

title: mistralai/timestral repository README
note: Fetched (also a research source). Standalone inference code, Apache-2.0; weights separate under Modified MIT. Says that at launch the 209M model was first among pretrained and zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, on TIME (98 tasks) and on fev-bench (100 tasks). Forecast call takes past_covariates and known_covariates (context plus horizon) and categorical versions; CPU is enough.

title: mistralai/timestral repository README
note: Fetched. Evaluation setup as the README gives it: zero-shot, forecaster defaults, full history up to 32,768 steps. GIFT-Eval (97 configurations) used past covariates only; fev-bench (100 tasks) used past and known covariates; TIME (98 tasks) has no covariates. So known-future covariates entered the headline numbers only through fev-bench. Pull requests are not accepted; issues are.

title: Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models

title: Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models
note: Fetched. Names weather forecasts and holiday calendars as examples of known-future inputs, but the worked example is an imagined industrial plant; no load or weather experiment. Most training data was synthetic; post-training mixes real and synthetic data, the real sets unnamed. Speed: one day ahead from three weeks of 15-minute data in 17 ms (5M) to 113 ms (209M) on 8 CPU threads.

title: Timestral (arXiv full text, v1)
note: Fetched. Training: synthetic-only pretraining at 8,192 steps of context, then a shorter post-training on real plus synthetic data at 32,768 steps. The real datasets are not named and no data cutoff is given, so overlap with benchmark sets or with US load series cannot be checked from the paper. title: Timestral (arXiv full text, v1)
note: Fetched. Extra benchmark IND-Eval (187 industrial tasks in energy, manufacturing, transport), rerun by the authors themselves with context capped at 4,096: 209M first with error relative to seasonal naive of 0.646 (point) and 0.435 (probabilistic), against 0.697 and 0.469 for t0-gamma, about 7% lower; 123M and 28M next. Known-future covariates were used on fev-bench only.

title: LICENSE of mistralai/Timestral-209M
note: Fetched (also a research source). Modified MIT: MIT-style grant with attribution, plus a condition that no rights apply if the user's company or employer had more than 20 million dollars of global consolidated revenue in the preceding month; such users need a commercial licence from Mistral or its hosted service. So commercial use is allowed only below that revenue line.

title: Issue 7: upper quantiles blow up with sign-fixed, piecewise-constant known covariates
note: Fetched (also a research source). Open user report, 24 Oct 2026, with a reproduction: with a nearly constant positive known-future covariate (a price), the 209M model's top quantile reaches thousands on low-volume series while the median stays sane. Two triggers: the default symmetric averaging negates covariates, and a covariate flat over the whole context that first changes in the horizon.

title: Issue 7: upper quantiles blow up with sign-fixed, piecewise-constant known covariates
note: Fetched. Same report, M5 retail data, 2,469 daily series, 28 days ahead: after masking flat price rows, the 28M model with covariates scored 0.652 (WMAPE plus absolute bias) against 0.665 without covariates, 0.676 AutoARIMA and 0.663 untuned LightGBM. A user's own test of covariate use, not a rerun of the benchmarks. No maintainer reply visible in the fetched text.

title: DEV Community post: a reader's three small tests of Timestral
note: Fetched (also a research source). Independent blog test with a script: Paris daily maximum temperature, 14-day holdout from 6 Oct 2026, CPU. 209M with 158 days of context: MAE 6.489, worse than repeating the last value (5.636), 80% band covering 43%; with three years of context MAE 3.326 and 64% coverage. The 5M model came close to the 209M. One series, one origin.
